messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: P0 - ApexHealth (private VPC) - intermittent 502/timeout hitting customer NLB targets in us-east-1. Escalation to on-call required. Pager: devon_oncall

devon_oncall: picking this up. seeing spikes in 502s from ApexHealth tenancy since 04:12 UTC. start time approx 04:10. I have their dedicated pool + private VPC context. tagging neteng and SE.

ben_network: looking. I see NLB target health flapping for target-group tg-apex-1 between Healthy/Unhealthy. Backend (ALB -> redwood-instances) shows high connection reset rate. Could be SG change or conntrack exhaustion on NATs.

carla_se: customer reports errors across multiple services - ingestion and chat endpoints. They see increased latency and 502s approx 04:10-04:20. No config changes on customer side. They use our Private package with private control plane, ALB in front of host pool, NLB for cross-VPC egress.

devon_oncall: quick checklist: 1) Were there infra deploys? 2) Any SG/routing changes rolled? 3) NATGateway metrics? 4) NLB healthcheck config?

ops-rotations-bot: deploy-bot: A deploy to infra/routing was merged at 03:58 UTC (infra/routing: update-sg-default-timeout) by aj. Rollout stage: canary. 

ben_network: that 03:58 deploy touched tenant-security-group default egress rule — it added a stricter ephemeral port range to outbound. I'm pulling cloudtrail and SG diff.

emma_sre: checking VPC flow logs and NLB healthcheck results. Noting a lot of TCP RSTs from the private worker instances to NLB healthcheck IPs, and conntrack table nearing capacity on the NAT instances. NAT->internet egress looks saturated for ephemeral ports.

frank_support: ApexHealth wants impact estimate for SLA. They report some 4xx/5xx across users. I told them we have a team on it and we may open a maintenance window.

devon_oncall: initial mitigation plan: A) revert the recent SG tightening for this tenant only (policy allows per-tenant override), B) temporarily bump conntrack on NAT/bastions or shift egress through standby NAT, C) add NLB target group healthcheck retries tolerance and set weight 0 to failover pool if needed, D) low-ttl DNS weighted shift if cross-region failover required. We'll coordinate order: revert SG -> monitor -> conntrack scaling -> routing fallback if not recovered.

ben_network: starting SG revert for apex-tenant-sg (tenant ID: apex-123). Applying rollback: restore ephemeral outbound 32768-60999 allowed. Patch in progress.

ops-rotations-bot: infra-bot: Change applied to security-group apex-tenant-sg by ben_network at 04:32 UTC - rule restored.

emma_sre: after SG rollback, healthchecks recovered for ~70% targets within 2 minutes. Connection resets decreased. However a subset of hosts still show conntrack exhaustion and old connections. I'm seeing NAT conntrack count at 96% on nat-az-b, and high TIME_WAIT backlog.

devon_oncall: ok, please scale conntrack and move a portion of egress to nat-standby. ben, can you shift a small portion of the tenant's route table to nat-standby to relieve nat-az-b? That should be low-risk.

ben_network: rerouting 10% of egress by adding a secondary route target to nat-standby via a temporary policy. Actioned at 04:41 UTC.

frank_support: I updated ApexHealth that we've restored most traffic and are performing egress smoothing. They asked for a timeline for full recovery.

carla_se: customer logs show gradual decline in 502s since 04:35. We'll keep monitoring. Also want to note: their ALB idle-timeout was 60s while NLB healthchecks are more aggressive; recommended align to avoid premature closes.

devon_oncall: good catch. Let's align ALB idle-timeout to 120s for this tenant while we stabilize. Will make a tenant-scoped config change.

ops-rotations-bot: config-bot: ALB idle-timeout for apex-123 set to 120s by devon_oncall at 04:47 UTC.

emma_sre: conntrack metrics back to 45% on nat-az-b after route shift and conntrack bump. NLB target group health shows all targets Healthy by 04:49. Latency back to baseline.

ben_network: I recommend a follow-up: increase NAT pool size for this tenant (longer term) and add connection reuse at the worker level. Also add automated runbook step: if SG changes are pushed to infra, skip tenant-scope hardening until confirmed.

devon_oncall: Agreed. For now, we'll keep monitoring for 30m. carla, frank — please coordinate an incident summary and customer follow-up. Also file an infra postmortem ticket for the deploy causing SG tightening.

frank_support: opened INC-APEX-2026-01 and notified account team. Sent customer message: "We've mitigated and restored service; follow-up with root cause analysis and actions."

carla_se: assembling timeline: 03:58 deploy to infra/routing changed tenant SG behavior -> 04:10 errors start -> 04:32 SG revert applied -> 04:41 egress smoothing -> 04:47 ALB idle-timeout adjusted -> 04:49 healthy. Will include traffic graphs and CloudTrail diffs in the postmortem.

devon_oncall: final status: Service restored, no current customer errors, keeping on-call watch for 30m. Postmortem owner assigned to ben_network. If any regression, re-page P0. Closing thread updates in 30m.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to: mitigated. Incident severity: P1 (downgraded from P0). Notes: SG rollback and egress smoothing resolved issue.

ben_network: creating follow-up JIRA: INFRA-4821 "Prevent auto-hardening SG rollout for private-tenants; add canary skip list" and assigning to infra team.

frank_support: customer acceptance: ApexHealth confirmed degraded window but accepts mitigation. Asked for formal RCA within 48 hours. I've scheduled a call.

carla_se: tagging postmortem: will include specific commands used, cloudtrail snapshots, and recommended config guardrails.

devon_oncall: thanks everyone. handing off to next on-call (emma_sre) at 05:10 UTC. I will add runbook notes.

ops-rotations-bot: shift-handoff: devon_oncall -> emma_sre at 05:10 UTC.

emma_sre: taking watch. I'll keep this monitored and will escalate if metrics deviate.

(END THREAD)
